author: omarQ8
quote: Dark Souls 3 is easily one of FromSoftware’s finest games. The combat is fast, smooth, and responsive, and the boss quality is arguably the best in the entire Dark Souls trilogy. Bosses like Abyss Watchers, Nameless King, Twin Princes, and Slave Knight Gael are unforgettable, both mechanically and **** atmosphere is incredible. The dying world of Lothric perfectly captures the feeling of a civilization reaching its end. The soundtrack is phenomenal, and the DLCs provide a fantastic conclusion to the trilogy.However, the game isn’t flawless. The world is noticeably more linear than the previous entries, exploration feels less rewarding at times, and some areas lack the creativity of Dark Souls 1 and 2. Build variety is solid, but the faster combat tends to favor certain playstyles.Despite these flaws, Dark Souls 3 delivers an incredible balance of challenging combat, memorable bosses, beautiful environments, and emotional storytelling. It’s not necessarily the most innovative Souls game, but it’s arguably the most polished and satisfying conclusion the trilogy could have received.

The hitboxes can be frustrating, and some areas rely too heavily on enemy placement. But despite its flaws, Dark Souls 2 has its own identity and isn’t afraid to experiment with new **** atmosphere, exploration, freedom, and sense of adventure make it a special experience.
